recent_items.title: Westminster Confession of Faith Ch.1 Sec.9
recent_items.description:
Chapter 1: Of the Holy Scripture Section 9 The infallible rule of interpretation of Scripture is the Scripture itself; and therefore, when there is a question about the true and full sense of any scripture (which is not manifold, but one), it must be searched and known by other places that speak more clearly.[1]
Scripture References: [1] Acts.15.15, 2Pet.1.20-2Pet.1.21

recent_items.title: Heidelberg Catechism Q7
recent_items.description:
Q7. From where, then, did man's depraved nature come? A. From the fall and disobedience of our first parents, Adam and Eve, in Paradise, for there our nature became so corrupt that we are all conceived and born in sin.
Scripture References: [1] Gen.3 [2] Rom.5.12,Rom.5.18-Rom.5.19 [3] Ps.51.5

recent_items.title: Westminster Shorter Catechism Q6
recent_items.description: Q6. How many persons are there in the Godhead? A. There are three persons in the Godhead; the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost; and these three are one God, the same in substance, equal in power and glory.

recent_items.title: Second Helvetic Confession Ch.4 Sec.1
recent_items.description: Chapter 4: Of Idols or Images of God, Christ and The Saints Section 1 IMAGES OF GOD Since God as Spirit is in essence invisible and immense, he cannot really be expressed by any art or image. For this reason we have no fear pronouncing with Scripture that images of God are mere lies. Therefore we reject not only the idols of the Gentiles, but also the images of Christians.

recent_items.title: Westminster Larger Catechism Q11
recent_items.description:
Q11. How doth it appear that the Son and the Holy Ghost are God equal with the Father? A. The scriptures manifest that the Son and the Holy Ghost are God equal with the Father, ascribing unto them such names, attributes, works, and worship, as are proper to God only.

recent_items.title: Puritan Catechism Q5
recent_items.description:
Q5. Are there more Gods than one? A. There is but one only, the living and true God.
Scripture References: [1] Deut.6.4 [2] Jer.10.10

recent_items.title: Westminster Confession of Faith Ch.1 Sec.10
recent_items.description:
Chapter 1: Of the Holy Scripture Section 10 The Supreme Judge, by which all controversies of religion are to be determined, and all decrees of councils, opinions of ancient writers, doctrines of men, and private spirits, are to be examined, and in whose sentence we are to rest, can be no other but the Holy Spirit speaking in the Scripture.[1]

recent_items.title: Second Helvetic Confession Ch.4 Sec.2
recent_items.description: Chapter 4: Of Idols or Images of God, Christ and The Saints Section 2 IMAGES OF CHRIST Although Christ assumed human nature, yet he did not on that account assume it in order to provide a model for carvers and painters. He denied that he had come "to abolish the law and the prophets" (Matt. 5:17). But images are forbidden by the law and the prophets" (Deut. 4:15; Isa. 44:9). He denied that his bodily presence would be profitable for the Church, and promised that he would be near us by his Spirit forever (John 16:7). Who, therefore, would believe that a shadow or likeness of his body would contribute any benefit to the pious? (II Cor. 5:5). Since he abides in us by his Spirit, we are therefore the temple of God (I Cor. 3:16). But "what agreement has the temple of God with idols?" (II Cor. 6:16).
